adminSrcNews.title: News Sources
adminSrcNews.subtitle: Configure the sources to crawl news from (replaces sources.yaml)
adminSrcNews.guide_s1_title: Standard workflow for adding a new source
adminSrcNews.guide_s1_i1: Fill in the Basic information group (Name, Domain, Tier, Region, Category).
adminSrcNews.guide_s1_i2: Pick the correct Source type in the Crawl configuration group, then fill in the matching URL.
adminSrcNews.guide_s1_i3: Click "Test configuration" — this step is mandatory before Saving.
adminSrcNews.guide_s1_i4: If the test returns junk links or misses articles → go back and adjust the Filters group, then test again.
adminSrcNews.guide_s1_i5: When the returned article list looks right → optionally fill in Metadata, then click Save.
adminSrcNews.guide_s2_i1: Source name: make it clear and distinguishable from other entries on the same domain — e.g. "EIA – Today in Energy" rather than just "EIA" (one domain can have several rows, each for a separate page/section). The name must be unique across the whole system.
adminSrcNews.guide_s2_i2: Domain: the root domain only, WITHOUT https:// or www. — e.g. eia.gov, not https://www.eia.gov. Used to keep the crawl from straying to other sites and to rate-limit requests per domain.
adminSrcNews.guide_s2_i3: Category: an internal label to classify the SOURCE (not the topic of each article) — free-form, but try to reuse existing labels (e.g. energy_official, financial_press, vn_press) to make filtering/statistics easier later.
adminSrcNews.guide_s2_i4: Tier: A = official agencies/exchanges (EIA, OPEC, ICE...); B = reputable press/organizations; C = aggregator sources with lower reliability.
adminSrcNews.guide_s2_i5: Region: International or Vietnam — determines which group articles from this source fall into in reports.
adminSrcNews.guide_s2_i6: Active: turn off to pause crawling this source without deleting it (the configuration is kept so you can re-enable it later).
adminSrcNews.guide_s2_i7: Run at 12:00: only enable for truly important Tier A sources that need an extra midday update — most sources should stay off; enabling it everywhere makes the 12:00 crawl run unnecessarily long.
adminSrcNews.guide_s3_title: Group 2 — Crawl configuration (choose the right Source type)
adminSrcNews.guide_s3_i1: html: a page with an article listing but NO RSS feed. Listing URL is required — paste the exact listing page URL (not the generic homepage if there is a dedicated news section).
adminSrcNews.guide_s3_i2: rss: a site with an RSS/Atom feed. RSS URL is required. Prefer this type when the source has a feed, as it is more stable and less likely to be blocked than HTML scraping.
adminSrcNews.guide_s3_i3: bloomberg_rss: used only for Bloomberg (handles multiple feeds + Google News link resolution) — the Bloomberg Feeds list is required, one URL per line.
adminSrcNews.guide_s3_i4: Max articles per crawl: leave empty to use the default (25). Set it lower for sites that publish a lot, to save requests on each crawl.
adminSrcNews.guide_s3_i5: Use Playwright: only enable when the page is an SPA/React/Next.js app that needs JS to show content, or when "Test configuration" returns 0 articles even though the URL is definitely correct. Do not enable by default — it uses more resources and is much slower than a plain fetch. It has no effect on RSS sources.
adminSrcNews.guide_s4_title: Group 3 — Filters (only needed when the test result is not clean)
adminSrcNews.guide_s4_i1: Article link regex: use when the default filter (requires URLs with 3 or more path levels) picks up non-article links or misses real articles. Write it to match the real article URL structure of the site — e.g. /todayinenergy/detail\.php or /pr-detail/. Always re-run Test configuration after changing this regex.
adminSrcNews.guide_s4_i2: Excluded paths: list extra path segments that are definitely NOT articles (tag/category/author/login/search pages...) if the system defaults are not enough for this site. Leave empty if there is no special need.
adminSrcNews.guide_s5_i1: Group: internal topic group numbers, used for filtering/statistics later — enter as "1, 3".
adminSrcNews.guide_s5_i2: Confidence: a subjective rating of how stable the URL is — sources marked "low" should have their crawl logs checked more often since the site is likely to change its structure.
adminSrcNews.guide_s5_i3: Internal note: record why this URL was chosen, previous URL changes, or special remarks — so the next person (including you in a few months) does not have to guess from scratch.
adminSrcNews.guide_s6_title: How to read the "Test configuration" (Test Crawl) result
adminSrcNews.guide_s6_i1: Always click this button BEFORE Saving — the system runs a real crawl with the current configuration (nothing is saved to the DB and Claude is not called, so there is no cost) and returns up to 5 articles found.
adminSrcNews.guide_s6_i2: If you see a list of articles with sensible titles/links pointing to real articles → the configuration is correct and you can click Save.
adminSrcNews.guide_s6_i3: If it reports "No articles could be crawled": open the Listing URL/RSS URL directly in a browser to check the link is right; if it is and still no articles appear, try enabling Use Playwright (the page may need JS or block bots).
adminSrcNews.guide_s6_i4: If the test returns links that are not articles (section links, tag pages...) → go back to the Filters group, add an Article link regex or Excluded paths, then test again.
adminSrcNews.guide_s7_i1: Choosing a Source type that does not match the URL you have — e.g. the site has an RSS feed but you leave the type as html and paste the RSS URL into the Listing URL field.
adminSrcNews.guide_s7_i2: Using a Source name that already exists — the system requires names to be unique and will return a 409 error on Save.
adminSrcNews.guide_s7_i3: Entering a Domain with https:///www. — enter the root domain only.
adminSrcNews.guide_s7_i4: Enabling "Run at 12:00" for too many sources that do not really need it, making the midday crawl run longer than necessary.
adminSrcNews.guide_s7_i5: Skipping the "Test configuration" step and saving right away — it is easy to create a source that never crawls any article without you noticing until the real crawl.

cbamEstimate.title: CBAM price estimate {quarter}
cbamEstimate.subtitle: Quarterly CBAM certificate price = VWAP of all primary EUA auctions on EEX · data to {date}

reason.quarter_fixed: All auctions of the quarter are done — the quarterly price is effectively fixed, awaiting EC publication.
reason.quarter_not_started: No auction yet this quarter — no reference to compare against; lock the core share only, as planned.
reason.quarter_mostly_fixed: Over {fixed}% of the quarter's volume is fixed — the open part is small; lock the core share only and focus on next quarter.
reason.spot_below_qtd: EUA is {gap}% below the fixed VWAP (threshold {threshold}%) → lock the tactical part (≤20% of the unfixed volume) with futures now — a trading view.
reason.spot_above_qtd: EUA is {gap}% above the fixed VWAP (threshold {threshold}%) → leave the tactical part (≤20% of the unfixed volume) unlocked until the price nears the VWAP; the core is still locked as planned.
reason.spot_near_qtd: EUA is {gap}% from the fixed VWAP (below the {threshold}% threshold) — lock the core share as planned; no tactical part.

cbamEstimate.upcoming: Next 7 days: {count} auctions ({from}–{to}), {volume} Mt in total
cbamEstimate.hedgeHow: {open}% of the quarter's CBAM obligation (tCO₂, weighted by remaining auction volume) is not yet priced and floats with the VWAP of the remaining auctions. Buy Dec EUA futures now for the core = {core}% of the quarterly CBAM obligation ({corePct}% of the unfixed part), then sell them down in line with the remaining auction schedule → futures P&L ≈ VWAP − purchase price, net cost ≈ today's purchase price. Buying EUAs along the schedule does not lock the cost.
cbamEstimate.productTitle: CBAM cost per tonne of product
cbamEstimate.productAssumed: Reported emissions are assumed — replace with verified actual figures.
cbamEstimate.formulaLegend: reported emissions − CBAM factor × CSCF × CBAM benchmark by CN code
cbamEstimate.productDefaultsIllustrative: Default values apply by country of origin — these figures are illustrative only and do not apply to Vietnamese-origin goods.
cbamEstimate.method: The EC's quarterly CBAM price = volume-weighted average (VWAP) of clearing prices of all primary EUA auctions on EEX in the quarter. Volumes not yet auctioned are assumed at the current EUA price; the confidence interval uses the EUA's realised daily volatility of {vol}% (random walk). This is an estimate, not the official price.
cbamEstimate.productNote: Direct emissions only (CBAM scope for aluminium/steel); remaining free-allocation factor {factor}% in {year}. Caveats: (1) these are 2021–2025 benchmarks — the 2026–2030 benchmarks have been updated and are usually lower, so the actual cost may be higher (not yet checked by CN code); (2) using EC default values instead of verified actual emissions usually raises the cost significantly — every +0.1 tCO₂/t of embedded emissions ≈ +EUR {per01}/t of product.
cbamEstimate.productNoteCbam: Deduction = CBAM factor {factor}% in {year} × CSCF × CBAM benchmark by CN code ({source}{verified}). Direct emissions only (CBAM scope for aluminium/steel); reported emissions are assumed. Every +0.1 tCO₂/t ≈ +EUR {per01}/t of product — the gap between actual and default values is what emission verification is worth.
cbamEstimate.productUnverified: (secondary-source figures — check against the regulation's annex)

forecastReview.rules: Grading rules: Right/Wrong once the order hits its target/stop or after {horizon} sessions (1–2 week window); before that only On track/Diverging. Direction counts as right when |%Δ| ≥ {dir}%; "sideways" is right when |%Δ| < {side}% AND every close in the window stays within {path}% of the reference. Pending orders are valid for {valid} sessions and cancelled if the price hits the target before filling; a limit order gapped through at the open fills at the open. Target reached before filling → "Right direction, not filled", excluded from the hit rate. Sunday/Monday reports are news-only, so there is no forecast to grade.

userConnect.title: Connect Claude Desktop
userConnect.intro: Set up once, then highlight a passage in a report and click Ask Claude: Claude Desktop automatically pulls the excerpt and the system's data to handle demanding tasks (generating PDF/Excel files, building strategies...). Results stay in Claude Desktop and are not saved back to the system.
userConnect.userOnly: This feature is only available to user accounts (email sign-in), not admin accounts.
userConnect.step1Title: Install the uv tool (once per machine)
userConnect.step1Open: Open {shell} and run the command below. Claude Desktop must already be installed on the machine.
userConnect.step1After: After installing, open a new {shell} window and run {cmd} to get the path of uvx — you will need it in step 3.
userConnect.step2Desc: The token lets Claude Desktop read report data on your behalf (read-only, expires after 90 days, can be revoked at any time). Use a separate token for each machine.
userConnect.newTokenNotice: New token — copy it now, it will not be shown again after you leave this page:
userConnect.step3Title: Add the connection to Claude Desktop
userConnect.step3Desc: In Claude Desktop: Settings → Developer → Edit Config (or open the file {path} directly), then paste the snippet below. If the file already has mcpServers, just add the carbon-analyst entry inside it.
userConnect.uvxPathLabel: Path to uvx on your machine
userConnect.macPathHint: macOS needs the full path (the output of which uvx) because the app does not use the Terminal's PATH.
userConnect.replacePlaceholder: Replace {placeholder} with the token from step 2 (create a new token above to have this snippet filled in automatically).
userConnect.step4a: Fully quit Claude Desktop (not just close the window) and reopen it.
userConnect.step4b: A tools icon will appear in the chat box; open it and if you see carbon-analyst, you are connected.
userConnect.step4c: Open a report, highlight the passage you want to ask about, click Ask Claude, choose a task type, submit the request, then paste the prompt into Claude Desktop. The first time, Claude will ask permission to use the tool — choose allow.
userConnect.mobileTitle: Use on your phone (Claude mobile / claude.ai)
userConnect.mobileDesc: Nothing to install. Create a token in step 2, then add the URL below as a custom connector: claude.ai → Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector (connectors added on the web also appear in the mobile app).
userConnect.mobileNeedToken: The URL is only shown right after you create a token in step 2 (the raw token cannot be retrieved later). Create a new token to get it.
userConnect.mobileWarn: This URL contains your token — treat it like a password and don't share it. If it leaks, revoke the token in step 2 and the URL stops working immediately.
userConnect.mobileNote: The phone connection doesn't remember a handoff's report between questions; Claude passes the report date itself when calling tools.

adminKnowledge.title: Knowledge documents
adminKnowledge.subtitle: Upload PDF (with a text layer) or Word (.docx) documents as background knowledge for Jenny: the system extracts the text, splits it into passages and indexes them. When generating the report, each selected section receives at most a few of the most relevant passages (cited by document name); Jenny chat looks them up when a question needs them. Documents are NOT sent to Claude Desktop/mobile.
